newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SING TAO -- S.Y. Chung, a member of post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa's inner cabinet, criticised the government for refusing to cooperate with Tung's office, which he said had put the future Chief Executive in an awkward situation.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Li Youwei, the Communist Party secretary of the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, said the governor of the People's Bank of China had instructed that the city would gradually allow foreign banks to conduct domestic currency business.

-- WEN WI PO -- China, Russia and three ex-Soviet Central Asian states signed a border troops agreement in Moscow. The leaders of the five countries expressed the wish to join hands to fight against separatism.
-- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said Beijing understood Moscow's worries over the expansion of NATO and that the Sino-Russian relationship meant neither alliance nor antagonism.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- More than 7,000 journalists from nearly 480 media organisations worldwide had registered to report on events surrounding Hong Kong's handover to China at midnight on June 30.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Attempts by Hong Kong clothing retailer Giordano International to revive its troubled China operations were scuppered when five state enterprises backed away from a proposed share placement.

-- The dramatic influx of investors into China's highly volatile stock markets since January has prompted the national securities watchdog to launch the first nationwide campaign to improve risk awareness and control.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A senior Stock Exchange of Hong Kong official told a High Court trial the exchange had no rules regarding conflict of interest.
-- Hong Kong's Official Receiver's office said the incidence of company insolvency and individual bankruptcy was rising due to a tougher business environment.
